title: CEO Interview with Manu Gulati of Velaura AI
gist: Velaura AI, a March 2026 spin-out of blockchain-chip maker Auradine led on development by ex-NUVIA co-founder Manu Gulati, is building clean-sheet, low-power silicon for premium Physical AI (robots, drones, humanoids) plus IP/design platform for hyperscaler custom AI processors, arguing that perf-per-watt, latency and integrated safety — not borrowed data-center or mobile architectures — gate real deployment.

insights.claim: Velaura AI spun out of Auradine in March 2026, repurposing energy-efficient silicon expertise originally developed for blockchain computing toward AI compute.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Bitcoin-mining ASIC know-how is being redeployed into AI edge silicon — a template for other crypto-ASIC teams pivoting to AI.
insights.quote: We spun out of Auradine in March 2026, building on energy-efficient silicon expertise developed for blockchain computing.

insights.claim: Velaura AI's Chief Development Officer Manu Gulati previously co-founded NUVIA, which Qualcomm acquired for roughly $1.5B, and held silicon roles at Apple, Google and Qualcomm.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Pedigree of the NUVIA team raises the odds Velaura becomes an acquisition target or credible Physical AI silicon entrant.

insights.claim: Velaura AI pursues a dual market: purpose-built Physical AI chips for premium robots and drones, and low-power IP plus a design platform for hyperscalers building their own AI processors.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The hyperscaler custom-silicon IP line gives a nearer-term revenue path while robotics demand matures.
insights.quote: Alongside Physical AI, we’re applying our low-power expertise to IP and a design platform for hyperscalers developing their own AI processors.

insights.claim: Velaura AI argues that power increasingly determines what is possible in AI, and its data center work targets getting more AI compute from the available power — the same problem as edge robotics at a different scale.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Perf-per-watt is the shared bottleneck from edge to data center; watch power-efficiency-first architectures for share gains.
insights.quote: We saw an opportunity to apply that foundation to AI, where power increasingly determines what’s possible.

insights.claim: Battery-powered robots and drones face limited space for cooling and batteries, so a machine that works briefly then spends hours charging has limited practical value — making compute efficiency directly tied to usefulness.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Edge AI chip winners will be judged on battery runtime impact, not peak TOPS.
insights.quote: A machine that works briefly and then spends hours charging has limited practical value.
insights.locator: At the same time, many robots

insights.claim: In drones, reducing heat from compute lowers required cooling hardware and thus weight, while in mobile robots higher compute efficiency allows more intelligence within the battery budget.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: System-level savings (cooling, weight, battery) are the value pitch for low-power edge AI silicon.
insights.locator: For a mobile robot, greater compute efficiency

insights.claim: Physical AI customers need inference onboard because cloud offloading adds latency and connectivity dependence; a dropped connection or late response degrades both usefulness and safe reaction.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Supports demand for on-device AI accelerators in robotics rather than cloud-robotics architectures.
insights.quote: Offloading computation to the cloud can introduce delays and dependence on connectivity.
insights.locator: They also need that performance onboard.

insights.claim: A robot that takes minutes to do what a person does in seconds is a demo, not a business; Physical AI customers need enough onboard intelligence and speed to deliver real productivity.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Discount robotics hype that lacks cycle-time parity with humans; latency/compute is the gating factor.
insights.quote: a robot that takes several minutes to complete something a person can do in seconds may be an interesting demonstration, but it’s difficult to build a business around it
insights.locator: As it applies to physical AI

insights.claim: Growing sophistication of world models and vision-language-action (VLA) models raises onboard compute demand for robots, which must turn perception into timely action within device power and thermal budgets.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Rising model complexity expands the TAM for edge AI silicon in robots.

insights.claim: Velaura AI claims many existing Physical AI compute solutions reuse architectures built for data centers or mobile devices, whereas it designs power, thermals, latency and safety into a clean-sheet architecture from the start.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Incumbent edge platforms derived from data-center/mobile designs may be vulnerable if purpose-built chips prove more efficient.
insights.quote: Many existing compute solutions draw on architectures originally developed for data centers or mobile devices.
insights.locator: What does the competitive landscape look like

insights.claim: Velaura AI targets industrial robotics, autonomous mobile robots, humanoids and commercial/industrial drones, and treats humanoids as a longer-term opportunity whose useful deployment is not yet proven.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Even a Physical AI chip vendor frames humanoids as long-dated; near-term revenue is in industrial robots and drones.
insights.quote: Humanoids are an exciting longer-term opportunity.

insights.claim: Physical AI customers' first concern is reliable, repeatable execution of their primary use case and economic feasibility; only after that do power, safety, compute and predictable latency become decisive.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Vendor selection in robotics silicon hinges on reliability and deployability before spec sheets.
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

insights.claim: Velaura AI positions integrated safety as working alongside intelligence so a machine can recognize a hazard, respond, and resume productive work, since these systems operate around people.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Hardware-level safety integration could become a differentiator/regulatory requirement for human-adjacent robots.
